page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpsv6 family, built on the arm64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and high memory bandwidth. The D32ps_v6 achieves top-tier results in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 450.97 GB/sec and write speeds of 188.48 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 66298.79 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19998.0. Database operations are efficient, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top tier. However, single-core performance and large-model LLM prompt processing, such as a 70B model at 4.64 tokens/sec, represent comparative bottlenecks, performing in the average and poor tiers respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides a high density of dedicated physical cores and top-tier memory bandwidth relative to its resource class. The absence of bundled local storage allows users to scale storage independently, optimizing resource allocation. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and Redis deployments. It is less suitable for workloads requiring specialized AVX or AMX instruction sets, or heavy single-threaded processing.
